import numpy as np

# Generate the sets using seed=53
rng = np.random.RandomState(53)
n_elements = 60
n_sets = 120
sets = []
for i in range(n_sets):
    size = rng.randint(5, 16)
    elements = sorted(rng.choice(n_elements, size, replace=False).tolist())
    cost = rng.randint(1, 20)
    sets.append((elements, cost))

# Greedy set cover algorithm
covered = set()
selected = [0] * 120
remaining_elements = set(range(60))

while remaining_elements:
    best_ratio = float('inf')
    best_set = -1
    
    for i in range(120):
        if selected[i] == 1:
            continue
            
        elements, cost = sets[i]
        new_elements = set(elements) & remaining_elements
        
        if len(new_elements) > 0:
            ratio = cost / len(new_elements)
            if ratio < best_ratio:
                best_ratio = ratio
                best_set = i
    
    if best_set == -1:
        break
        
    selected[best_set] = 1
    elements, cost = sets[best_set]
    new_covered = set(elements) & remaining_elements
    covered.update(new_covered)
    remaining_elements -= new_covered

# Add some low-cost sets for redundancy
for i in range(120):
    if selected[i] == 0 and sets[i][1] <= 3:  # Very low cost sets
        selected[i] = 1
